verses.zh: 大卫住在自己宫中，对先知拿单说：「看哪，我住在香柏木的宫中，耶和华的约柜反在幔子里。」
verses.en: When David had settled into his palace,[NOTE:1] he[NOTE:2] said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I am living in a palace[NOTE:3] made from cedar, while the ark of the Lord’s covenant is under a tent.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “David.” The pronoun “he” has been used in the translation here to avoid redundancy in keeping with contemporary English style.
Heb “house.”
Heb “tent curtains.”
verses.commentary:
17:1 "his house" This refers to David's palace (cf. 2 Sam. 5:11; 1 Chr. 14:1), built with materials and
craftsmen from Hiram, King of Tyre, a friend of David.

The "cedar" for David's palace came from Lebanon.

▣ "ark of the covenant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT.

▣ "under curtains" This refers to the tabernacle, described in Exodus 25-26.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHART OF THE TABERNACLE

verses.zh: 拿单对大卫说：「你可以照你的心意而行，因为　神与你同在。」
verses.en: Nathan said to David, “You should do whatever you have in mind,[NOTE:1] for God is with you.”
notes: Heb “all that is in your heart.”
verses.commentary:
17:2 How Nathan, the royal court prophet, received this initial revelation is not stated. Later he will receive
a divine reversal in a dream to David (cf. 1 Chr. 17:3-4). David will not build the temple (cf. 1 Chr. 28:23).

Note the IMPERATIVES of God's word.

- 1 Chr. 17:2, "do" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE

- 1 Chr. 17:4, "go" ‒ BDB 229, KB 241, Qal IMPERATIVE

Possibly Nathan assumed to know God's will without asking or God made a later clarification. David
could plan and gather material but Solomon would build the temple with Hiram's materials and artisans.

verses.zh: 当夜，　神的话临到拿单，说：
verses.en: That night God told Nathan,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the word of God was [i.e., came] to Nathan.”
verses.commentary:
17:3 The OT Tyndale Commentary by Martin Selman (pp. 181-182) suggests that "the word of God"
mentioned in 1 Chr. 17:3-15, along with 2 Chr. 7:11-22, is the key theological theme around which the Chronicler
structures his book.

verses.zh: 「你去告诉我仆人大卫，说耶和华如此说：『你不可建造殿宇给我居住。
verses.en: “Go, tell my servant David: ‘This is what the Lord says: “You must not build me a house in which to live.
verses.commentary:
17:4 "My servant" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MY SERVANT.

▣ "you shall not build a house for Me to dwell in" The reason is stated in 1 Chr. 28:2-3; David was a man of war.

verses.zh: 自从我领以色列人出埃及，直到今日，我未曾住过殿宇，乃从这会幕到那会幕，从这帐幕到那帐幕。
verses.en: For I have not lived in a house from the time I brought Israel up from Egypt[NOTE:1] to the present day. I have lived in a tent that has been in various places.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “from Egypt” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

I have lived in a tent that has been in various places. The point here is that the Lord moved with the tabernacle as it moved from place to place; he did not confine himself to a particular location.tc Heb “and I was from tent to tent and from tabernacle.” The words אֶל־מִשְׁכָּן (ʾel mishkan, “to tabernacle”) should probably be added at the end of the sentence to complete this prepositional phrase and produce symmetry with the preceding prepositional phrase. The words probably fell from the text by homoioteleuton.
verses.commentary: 17:5 The parallel in 2 Sam. 7:6 specifically mentions "Egypt." The exodus is alluded to in 1 Chr. 17:21.

verses.zh: 凡我同以色列人所走的地方，我何曾向以色列的一个士师，就是我吩咐牧养我民的说：你为何不给我建造香柏木的殿宇呢？』
verses.en: Wherever I moved throughout Israel, I did not say[NOTE:1] to any of the leaders whom I appointed to care for my people Israel,[NOTE:2] ‘Why have you not built me a house made from cedar?’”’
notes: In the Hebrew text the statement is phrased as a rhetorical question (“Did I say a word?”) meaning “I did not say a word.”
Heb “to one of the judges of Israel whom I commanded to shepherd my people.”
verses.commentary:
17:6 "I have walked with all Israel" This is anthropomorphic language.

A temple for YHWH was not YHWH's idea or command, but a desire on David's part.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PROBLEMS AND LIMITATIONS OF HUMAN LANGUAGE

▣ "judges" The parallel in 2 Sam. 7:7 has "tribes" and the LXX has "tribes" here, but because "judges" are
mentioned specifically again in 1 Chr. 17:10, the MT is probably correct (AB, p. 124).

verses.zh: 现在你要告诉我仆人大卫，说万军之耶和华如此说：『我从羊圈中将你召来，叫你不再跟从羊群，立你作我民以色列的君。
verses.en: “So now, say this to my servant David: ‘This is what the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] says: “I took you from the pasture and from your work as a shepherd[NOTE:2] to make you a leader of my people Israel.
notes: Traditionally, “Lord of hosts.”
Heb “and from after sheep.”
verses.commentary:
17:7 "My servant David" See note at 1 Chr. 17:4.

▣ "the Lord of hosts" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord OF HOSTS.

▣ "I took you from the pasture. . ." This is an allusion to YHWH's choice of David from among the sons
of Jesse (cf. 1 Samuel 16).

David as a shepherd reflects biblical imagery (royal title).

- God as shepherd, Ps. 23:1 (see full note online); 80:2; Jer. 31:10; Ezek. 38:11-16

- Moses' successors, Num 27:17; 1 Kgs. 22:17; 2 Chr. 18:16

- Jesus (the Davidic Messiah) as shepherd, Isa. 40:11; Zechariah 10-12; John 10

verses.zh: 你无论往哪里去，我常与你同在，剪除你的一切仇敌；我必使你得大名，好像世上大大有名的人一样。
verses.en: I was with you wherever you went, and I defeated[NOTE:1] all your enemies before you. Now I will make you as famous as the great men of the earth.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cut off.”
Heb “and I will make for you a name like the name of the great men who are in the earth.”
verses.commentary:
17:8 "I have been with you wherever you have gone" What a great promise and spiritual reality for God's
presence and leadership!

Notice how YHWH's personal presence manifested itself.

- I have cut off all your enemies, 1 Chr. 17:8

- I will make you a name (similar to Gen. 12:1-3), 1 Chr. 17:8

- I will appoint a place (i.e., land) for My people Israel, 1 Chr. 17:9

- I will plant them

- they will dwell in their own place

- they will be moved no more

- the wicked shall not waste them any more

- I will subdue all your enemies, 1 Chr. 17:10

- I will build you a house (i.e., dynasty), 1 Chr. 17:10

- I will establish your sons (i.e., Solomon and his seed) on the throne forever, 1 Chr. 17:12-14

verses.zh: 我必为我民以色列选定一个地方，栽培他们，使他们住自己的地方，不再迁移；凶恶之子也不像从前扰害他们，
verses.en: I will establish a place for my people Israel and settle[NOTE:1] them there; they will live there and not be disturbed[NOTE:2] anymore. Violent men will not oppress them again, as they did in the beginning[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “plant.”
Heb “shaken.”
Heb “and sons of violence will no longer consume them as in the beginning.”
verses.commentary:
17:9 "will plant them" This is imagery of Israel as a grape plant.

- she was transplanted from Egypt (cf. Psalm 80)

- planted in the Promised Land (cf. Exod. 15:17; 2 Sam. 7:10; Ps. 44:2)

- she brought forth bad grapes (cf. Isaiah 5; Jer. 2:21; 11:17; 12:2)

- she was uprooted and transplanted in Mesopotamia (cf. Isa. 5:2,7; Jer. 45:4; 32:36-44)

- YHWH will plant her again in Canaan, never to be uprooted again (cf. 1 Chr. 17:9; Jer. 24:6; Ezek. 34:25-31; Amos 9:15)

▣ "the wicked" The MT has "sons of wickedness." This idiom is also found in 2 Sam. 7:10; Ps. 89:22.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "SONS OF. . ." (OT)

verses.zh: 并不像我命士师治理我民以色列的时候一样。我必治服你的一切仇敌，并且我―耶和华应许你，必为你建立家室。
verses.en: and during the time when I appointed judges to lead my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies.“‘“I declare to you that the Lord will build a dynastic house[NOTE:1] for you!
notes: Here the word “house” is used in a metaphorical sense, referring to a royal dynasty. The Lord’s use of the word here plays off the literal sense that David had in mind as he contemplated building a temple (“house”) for the Lord. In the translation the adjective “dynastic” is supplied to indicate that the term is used metaphorically.

verses.zh: 你寿数满足归你列祖的时候，我必使你的后裔接续你的位，我也必坚定他的国。
verses.en: When the time comes for you to die,[NOTE:1] I will raise up your descendant,[NOTE:2] one of your own sons, to succeed you, and I will establish his kingdom.
notes: Heb “and it will be when your days are full to go with your ancestors.”
Heb “your seed.”
verses.commentary:
17:11 "When your days are fulfilled" This VERB (BDB 569, KB 583, Qal
PERFECT) is an idiom for the appointed days of a person's life, here David's (cf. 2 Sam. 7:12). Also note its
usage in Lam. 4:18. Believers' lives are in the hand of God (cf. Matt. 6:25-34; 10:29-31), not a result of luck, fate, chance, or
a capricious spiritual entity.

▣ "go to be with your fathers" The LXX has "lie down" or "sleep," which translated the Hebrew idiom
for death (i.e., "sleep," cf. 2 Sam. 7:12).

▣ "I will establish his kingdom" In context this refers to Solomon, but in the larger message of the Bible,
it refers to Jesus, the Davidic Messiah (cf. Mark 1:11; Luke 1:32-33; Heb. 1:5).

verses.zh: 他必为我建造殿宇；我必坚定他的国位直到永远。
verses.en: He will build me a house, and I will make his dynasty permanent.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and I will establish his throne permanently.”
verses.commentary:
17:12 "He shall build for Me a house" This refers to Solomon. 1 Kings 8 records Solomon's wonderful
dedicatory prayer. He clearly understood the purpose of YHWH's temple.

verses.zh: 我要作他的父，他要作我的子；并不使我的慈爱离开他，像离开在你以前的扫罗一样。
verses.en: I will become his father, and he will become my son. I will never withhold my loyal love from him, as I withheld it from the one who ruled before you.[NOTE:1]
notes: The one who ruled before you is a reference to Saul, from whom the kingdom was taken and given to David.
verses.commentary:
17:13 "I will be his father" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FATHERHOOD OF GOD and
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SON OF GOD.

▣ "My lovingkindness" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: LOVINGKINDNESS (hesed).

YHWH will not take away His Spirit from Solomon as He did with Saul (cf. 1 Sam. 16:14,23; 18:12;
28:15). The parallel in 2 Sam. 7:14 mentions Divine discipline instead of rejection.

However, one must also remember the conditional nature of YHWH's covenant with Israel (cf.
Jeremiah 7; 15:1-4; 16:5). YHWH's covenant demanded faith, obedience, and perseverance!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 我却要将他永远坚立在我家里和我国里；他的国位也必坚定，直到永远。』」
verses.en: I will put him in permanent charge of my house and my kingdom; his dynasty will be permanent.”’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and his throne will be established permanently.”
verses.commentary:
17:14 Notice that Solomon's kingdom is YHWH's Kingdom; the temple is YHWH's house (cf. 1 Chr. 28:5; 29:22;
2 Chr. 9:8; 13:8)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE KINGDOM OF GOD

▣ "forever" The term is repeated twice.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)

verses.zh: 拿单就按这一切话，照这默示告诉大卫。
verses.en: Nathan told David all these words that were revealed to him.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to all these words and according to all this revelation, so Nathan said to David.”

verses.zh: 于是大卫王进去，坐在耶和华面前，说：「耶和华　神啊，我是谁，我的家算甚么，你竟使我到这地步呢？
verses.en: King David went in, sat before the Lord, and said: “Who am I, O Lord God, and what is my family,[NOTE:1] that you should have brought me to this point?
notes: Heb “house.”
verses.commentary:
17:16 Apparently David entered the Tabernacle of the wilderness, which is described in Exodus 25-26. It
is surprising that David is said to "sit" before the Lord. It is found in 2 Sam. 7:18. It may be a metaphor for "tarrying"
before the Lord.

In 1 Chr. 17:16-18, David marvels at YHWH's love, care, and promotions of himself and his family.

verses.zh: 神啊，这在你眼中还看为小，又应许你仆人的家至于久远。耶和华　神啊，你看顾我好像看顾高贵的人。
verses.en: And you did not stop there, O God! You have also spoken about the future of your servant’s family.[NOTE:1] You have revealed to me what men long to know,[NOTE:2] O Lord God.
notes: Heb “and this was small in your eyes, O God, so you spoke concerning the house of your servant for a distance.”

The translation “You have revealed to me what men long to know” is very tentative; the meaning of the Hebrew text is unclear. The text appears to read literally, “and you see me like the searching of man, that which is upward,” which is nonsensical. The translation above assumes the following: (1) The Qal verb translated “you see me” is repointed as a Hiphil, “you showed me,” (2) תּוֹר (tor) is understood in the sense of “searching, exploring,” and (3) הַמַּעֲלָה (hammaʿalah) is taken in a temporal sense of “that which lies beyond.” Thus one could translate, “you have shown me what men search for, what lies beyond.”
verses.commentary:
17:17 The end of this verse is very ambiguous and uncertain in the MT. There are many suggestions but
no consensus among translations or scholars. The JPSOA has "You regard me as a man of distinction." The NET
Bible explains its emendations and assumptions of the translation ("You have revealed to me what man longs to know")
on p. 654, #30.

The MT has "as the turn of man and the step." The meanings of both "turn" (BDB 1064) and "step"
(BDB 752 II) are questionable. It is possible "turn" means "law" (see Robert B. Girdlestone, Synonyms of the Old
Testament, pp. 47-48).

verses.zh: 你加于仆人的尊荣，我还有何言可说呢？因为你知道你的仆人。
verses.en: What more can David say[NOTE:1] to you? You have honored your servant; you have given your servant special recognition.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “say” is supplied in the translation for clarification. The Hebrew verb means “add.”
Heb “for honoring your servant, and you, your servant, know.”
verses.commentary:
17:18 "honor" This is one usage of kabod (NIDOTTE, vol, 2, p. 580 [b]).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (kabod, OT)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你行了这大事，并且显明出来，是因你仆人的缘故，也是照你的心意。
verses.en: O Lord, for the sake of your servant and according to your will,[NOTE:1] you have done this great thing in order to reveal your greatness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “heart.”
Heb “to make known all the great deeds.”
verses.commentary:
17:19 David affirms the great mercy and power of YHWH. God's character (i.e., "mercy") and purposes
(i.e., "redemption,") are the theological keys to human history!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "for Your servant's sake" The parallel in 2 Sam. 7:21 has "for the sake of Your word."

▣ "all the greatness" See 2 Sam. 7:21, 23, which describe the great acts of God before and during the
exodus.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，照我们耳中听见，没有可比你的，除你以外再无　神。
verses.en: O Lord, there is none like you; there is no God besides you! What we heard is true![NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew text reads literally, “in all which we heard with our ears,” but בְּכֹל (bekhol, “in all”) should probably be emended to כְּכֹל (kekhol, “according to all”).
verses.commentary:
17:20 See
SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM.

verses.zh: 世上有何民能比你的民以色列呢？你　神从埃及救赎他们作自己的子民，又在你赎出来的民面前行大而可畏的事，驱逐列邦人，显出你的大名。
verses.en: And who is like your people, Israel, a unique nation[NOTE:1] in the earth? Their God[NOTE:2] went to claim[NOTE:3] a nation for himself! You made a name for yourself by doing great and awesome deeds[NOTE:4] when you drove out[NOTE:5] nations before your people whom you had delivered from the Egyptian empire and its gods.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “a nation, one.”
Heb “whose God,” or “because God.” In the Hebrew text this clause is subordinated to what precedes. The clauses are separated in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “redeem” or “deliver.”
Heb “to make for yourself a name [with] great and awesome [deeds].”
Heb “to drive out.”
Heb “from Egypt, nations.” The parallel text in 2 Sam 7:23 reads “from Egypt, nations and its gods.”
verses.commentary:
17:21 "redeem" This VERB is used twice in this verse. God formed Israel into a people based
on His promises to Abraham (i.e., Gen. 12:1-3; 15:21-22) and now through a Davidic covenant, which complements and
extends the Mosaic covenant. All are conditional on God's initiation and preservation. All are presented in a conditional
structure (i.e., obedience).

SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

▣ "by great and terrible things" This refers to YHWH's miraculous acts in delivering Israel from Egypt
(cf. 2 Sam. 7:23; Ps. 106:22).

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

verses.zh: 你使以色列人作你的子民，直到永远；你―耶和华也作他们的　神。
verses.en: You made Israel your very own nation for all time.[NOTE:1] You, O Lord, became their God.
notes: Heb “and you made your people Israel your own for a people permanently.”
verses.commentary:
17:22-24 "forever" This is a theological extension of 1 Chr. 17:12-14. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam)
for the conditional nature of "forever." Note also that the rejection of Saul mentioned in 2 Sam. 7:14-15, implies the conditional
nature of the royal promise. See D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks, "Conditional or Unconditional?" (pp. 44-47).

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你所应许仆人和仆人家的话，求你坚定，直到永远，照你所说的而行。
verses.en: So now, O Lord, may the promise you made about your servant and his family become a permanent reality![NOTE:1] Do as you promised,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and now, O Lord, the word which you spoke concerning your servant and concerning his house, may it be established permanently.”
Heb “as you have spoken.”
verses.commentary:
17:23 David prays (IMPERATIVE OF REQUEST) that God's plans for him and his seed be established.

- be established ‒ BDB 52, KB 63, Niphal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

- do as You have spoken ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal IMPERATIVE

The theological keys to the Davidic Covenant are the will and character of YHWH.

verses.zh: 愿你的名永远坚立，被尊为大，说：『万军之耶和华是以色列的　神，是治理以色列的　神。』这样，你仆人大卫的家必在你面前坚立。
verses.en: so[NOTE:1] it may become a reality[NOTE:2] and you may gain lasting fame,[NOTE:3] as people say,[NOTE:4] ‘The Lord of Heaven’s Armies is the God of Israel.’[NOTE:5] The dynasty[NOTE:6] of your servant David will be established before you,
notes: Following the imperative in v. 23b, the prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result: “so it might become a reality.”
Heb “so it might be established.”

Heb “and your name might be great permanently.” Following the imperative in v. 23b, the prefixed verbal form with vav conjunctive indicates purpose/result (parallel to the previous purpose/result clause): “[so]…you might gain lasting fame.”
Heb “saying.” The words “as people” are supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

Heb “the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, the Lord of hosts], the God of Israel, Israel’s God.” The phrases אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (ʾelohey yisraʾel, “God of Israel”) and אֱלֹהִים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (ʾelohim leyisraʾel, “Israel’s God”) are probably alternative readings that have been conflated in the text.
Heb “house.”
verses.commentary:
17:24 YHWH's name being great is the goal of all history! All of the Patriarchs and leaders of Israel are
meant to magnify YHWH's name! The latter part of 1 Chr. 17:27 may also refer to YHWH, not David.

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，因你启示仆人说，我必为你建立家室，所以仆人大胆在你面前祈祷。
verses.en: for you, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build a dynasty[NOTE:1] for him. That is why your servant has had the courage to pray to you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “That is why your servant found to pray before you.” Perhaps the phrase אֶת לִבּוֹ (ʾet libbo, “his heart”) should be supplied as the object of the verb “found.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，惟有你是　神，你也应许将这福气赐给仆人。
verses.en: Now, O Lord, you are the true God;[NOTE:1] you have made this good promise to your servant.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the God.” The article indicates uniqueness here.
Heb “and you have spoken to your servant this good thing.”
verses.commentary:
17:26 "You are God" This phrase has the DEFINITE ARTICLE, which denotes monotheism,
which is also alluded to in 1 Chr. 1:20.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

verses.zh: 现在你喜悦赐福与仆人的家，可以永存在你面前。耶和华啊，你已经赐福，还要赐福到永远。」
verses.en: Now you are willing to bless your servant’s dynasty[NOTE:1] so that it may stand permanently before you, for you, O Lord, have blessed it and it will be blessed from now on into the future.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “for you, O Lord, have blessed and [it is] blessed permanently.”
verses.commentary:
17:27 "bless" This VERB (BDB 138, KB 159) is used three times.

- Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- Piel PERFECT

- Pual PARTICIPLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: BLESSING (OT)

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why is this chapter crucial in the theology of Chronicles?

- Did Nathan make a false prophetic statement in 1 Chr. 17:2?

- Why did David want to build a house for the ark?

- Did God want a temple?

- What are the two meanings of the word "house" in 1 Chronicles 17?

- Why does Chronicles not mention God's discipline of David's descendants found in 2 Sam l 7?

- Is the Davidic covenant conditional or unconditional?

- Does 1 Chr. 17:20 affirm monotheism?

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is a crucial and powerful theological context. It is parallel to 2 Samuel 7. However, 2
Samuel 7 mentions YHWH's disciplining David's royal descendants when they sin, but
Chronicles ignores the waywardness of the Judean Kings. This text has no counterpoint to 2 Sam.
7:14-15 nor does it mention Saul's rejection.

- The God of Israel promises to establish the house/dynasty of David as King forever. This is the
essence of the Davidic Covenant. The Messiah will be a descendant of King David (cf. Matthew 1; Luke 3).

- This context obviously links to Jacob's tribal blessing of Genesis 49, about tribe Judah (cf. Gen. 49:8-12).

- The problem comes with the NT focus on "all humans," not just Israel.

- Notice the variety in God's names.

- God (Elohim), 1 Chr. 17:17,21,22,26

- Lord (YHWH), 1 Chr. 17:4,10,19,20,22,23,26,27

- Lord of hosts, 1 Chr. 17:7,24

- O Lord God (YHWH, Elohim), 1 Chr. 17:16,17

- the God of Israel (Eloah), 1 Chr. 17:24

- the God to Israel (Elohim), 1 Chr. 17:24
